title: Guava 33.6.0 now brings a warning when used with GWT (2.13)
body:
### Guava Version

33.6.0-jre

### Description

Guava 33.6.0 brings (via https://github.com/google/guava/commit/638ab1846d2e6e794b831f33cc063e6478a44040) now brings a warning when used with GWT (2.13)

` Warnings in com/google/common/collect/super/com/google/common/collect/ImmutableMap.java`
`  [WARN] Line 248: [unusable-by-js] Type of parameter 'entries' in 'ImmutableMap ImmutableMap.jsOfEntries(Map.Entry[])' is not usable by but exposed to JavaScript.`
`  [WARN] Suppress "[unusable-by-js]" warnings by adding a @SuppressWarnings("unusable-by-js") annotation to the corresponding member.`

Could you please add the @SuppressWarnings("unusable-by-js") to the method to avoid this warning, even if J2CL (and not GWT) is the (main) focus for Google?

### Example

```java
Use ImmutableMap in GWT code
```

### Expected Behavior

No warning (as before)

### Actual Behavior

Warning (quite confusing) when used with GWT

### Packages

com.google.common.collect

### Platforms

GWT

### Checklist

- [x] I agree to follow the [code of conduct](https://github.com/google/.github/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

- [x] I can reproduce the bug with the [latest](https://github.com/google/guava/releases/latest) version of Guava available.
